Ask in plain words: was weather a factor, what helped last time. It answers from your own logs.
Every trigger counts Low, Mild or High towards your score, and fades over the days after. Cross a line and your level changes. Adjust any of it by hand.
Garmin, Apple Watch, Polar, Oura, WHOOP and more
Log and track from your wearable

Once a week the AI proposes changes, like moving your gauge lines. Tick what you agree with.
Set your last period and cycle length. Risk rises around the predicted date.
Practitioners you can share your diary with, articles picked for you, and a forum of people like you.
Sleep, HRV, weather, cycle, food. Tap any card for the detail and the history.
Tap Log Migraine, or just talk. Triggers your watch and phone caught are already ticked, with the time they hit.
The gauge shows how full your bucket is: Low, Mild or High. Under it: the 7 day outlook.
Triggers, medicines, reliefs, how you felt. One pass through your day, tap what applies, done.
Tyramine, histamine, gluten and alcohol get flagged as you add a food.
Which triggers really matter, what helped, and a report you can hand your doctor.

_why: Pool-item vocabulary: canonical English labels seeded into every user's template pools (triggers, symptoms, medicines, reliefs, locations, activities, migraine types, wearable/auto-trigger metrics). The client translates them at render via t(label); the stored value stays English. Nothing in the Compose sources spells these out at a display site, so extract.py cannot scan them — they are declared here and merged into strings.json, which keeps them under the length gate and in the generated tables.
_budgets: class is hard because these render in chips and grid cells that cannot wrap; max_len is a flat 32, the widest such cell.
